At 10:00 a.m. on December 13, 2021, an employee was reading the identification
codes on Striker military vehicles that were loaded on a flatbed rail car when

was attempting to remove a patient (cat) from a kennel to provide Veterinarian
prescribed treatment. The animal had been examined shortly before being placed
in the kennel and was wrapped in a 'burrito' blanket to keep it calm; however,
the employee noted that the animal had urinated in the blanket. The employee

blanket. The animal rotated in the grasp of the employee and bit her right hand
thumb and index finger. The employee was seen in the Emergency Room where the
wound was cleaned and she was released with antibiotics on the same day. The
employee developed an infection and returned to the Emergency Room on December

thumb. This resulted in a laceration. The employee was hospitalized for
treatment.

between the mast and chain.  The employee was hospitalized to treat an
amputation of his left middle and ring fingers, and a laceration of his left

At 11:40 a.m. on November 17, 2021, an employee was pruning a mulberry tree at

hospitalization.

At 10:15 a.m. on December 13, 2021, an employee and a coworker arrived at a job
site to connect secondary electrical services to a transformer. The coworker
went to perform an initial job hazard analysis before the work could start and
left the employee at the transformer to wait. The employee was supposed to wait
but was confused and began pulling cables out in the transformer unaware that
the transformer was still live. The employee was in the transformer pulling
cables out when a metal wrench fell out of his pocket. The employee picked the
wrench up with his left hand and went to pull the last cable when the wrench
touched a live part in the transformer and created an arc flash. The employee

went back to the transformer and found the employee, made sure he was ok, and

beneath the employee and fell over and the employee also falling approximately
nine feet and landing on top of the ladder. The employee was hospitalized to
treat a compound fracture to the right lower leg.

the employee was removing the roller, his glove became caught in between an
adjacent roller and a free moving bearing. The employee jerked his arm away from
the machine and sustained a partial amputation of the left index finger. The
employee was treated without hospitalization.

pins of a shipping container using a hammer.  The employee's left hand was
beneath the container.  The pins locked and the container crushed the employee's
left hand, resulting in the amputation of his left pinky and severe damage to

responding to a report of a capsized canoe, the boat hit a tree growing out from

his seat landing inside the boat, was found unresponsive and in a fetal position

injuries sustained in the boat accident.  The other officer sustained a closed
fractured nose, closed head injury with concussion, a cerebral concussion and a
laceration to his left knee.  The Maine Warden Service accident investigation
and accident reconstruction report looked at several factors that may have
caused the boat accident by failing to negotiate the right hand sweeping turn in
the river. Information gathered from the Evinrude Engine Control Unit (ECU)
indicated the motor was running for 1 minute 59 seconds at 81%-82% throttle
position and quickly placed into neutral position in 1 second.  When the
throttle is placed in neutral with a jet type motor the boat loses all steering
capability. With the throttle positioned at 81%-82% the velocity equates to 27
and 33 miles per hour or between 39.6 feet per second and 48.4 feet per second.
As the boat entered the sweeping right hand turn, the officer had 7 to 9 seconds
with the tree in view prior to impact if the boat was on the right side of the
river. If the boat followed the deepest part of the river bringing him towards
the left side of the river, a tree was found 160.9 feet up river from the crash
site that was submerged below the rivers surface with what appeared to be fresh
damage. When the Warden Service arrived at the crash site they found the Police
boat anchored down river from the crash site, they believe the anchor was
deployed upon impact. Also noted were at least two v-shaped sticks wedged
between the motor and the transom of the boat which could have affected the
steering capability of the boat and could account for no evasive action prior to
impact.

his baseball cap activated the left side, causing the machine to cycle. His left
hand was crushed and lacerated. Employee #1 was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:15 p.m. on October 17, 2017, an employee was cleaning an auger while the
machine was on. The employee places a hand in the auger and sustained an
amputation of a finger on the right hand.

after filling the silo with corn silage when the silo tipped over.  Both
employees were inside the silo when it collapsed.  Employee #1 suffered several

At 7:45 a.m. on October 20, 2017, an employee was working for a firm that
manufactured wood pellets. He was operating a skid steer front end loader to

operator, the employee. The pellets caused the cab to collapse onto the operator
as well as engulfing the entire cab. When the narrative was written it had not

death. An autopsy was pending.

starting work and was resting in a bus while waiting for transportation.  The
employee had been talking normally and, after 5 minutes, leaned back, made a
snoring sound, and began convulsing.  Emergency Services was contacted and CPR
was performed until paramedics arrived and took over.  The employee died from
natural causes.
At 2:45 a.m. on October 21, 2017, a security guard was closing a sliding gate
after a truck left the yard. As the gate was closing, a stopper came off of its
guide and the gate fell on the security guard. The security guard was killed.
At 12:30 p.m. on October 23, 2017, Employee #1, employed by a construction

a concrete pumper when the pumper's outriggers shifted and sank into the ground.

Emergency services were called, and Employee #1 was transported to the hospital.
He was admitted and treated for a severe head injury causing memory loss, a
shattered foot which became infected and required amputation of the foot and
leg, and a fractured upper arm.
At 8:30 a.m. on October 6, 2017, an employee was positioning a kettle cradle on
a flatbed truck.  As the employee was pulling the cradle, one of the decayed
wooden boards came off of the cradle and the employee lost his balance, fell
approximately 5 feet, and landed on his radio.  The employee suffered multiple
fractures to include both wrists, several ribs, scrum, and pelvis.  The employee
also suffered a punctured lung and was hospitalized.
At 9:30 a.m. on September 15, 2017, an employee was cleaning a mixer.  The
employee reached into the mixer while it was running and his right hand was
caught, resulting in an amputation of the employee's right hand.  The employee
was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.
At 12:00 p.m. on October 9, 2017, am employee was working from a ladder to
replace the ballast of a light fixture. During work, the employee received an
electric shock and fell from the ladder. The employee sustained burns to one of
his fingers and multiple contusions, which he was hospitalized and received
treatment.
At 10:45 a.m. on October 9, 2017, an employee was removing a jam from a machine.
The employee amputated both hands when the press came down on top of his hands

At 9:30 a.m. on October 10, 2017, as per information gathered during the
interviews, the employee was sanding the walls in preparation for painting and

killed.

the roof, he stepped off the rake edge and fell to the ground below. The
employee sustained multiple injuries, including a broken collar bone and pelvis,
and had to have a chest tube inserted. Employee #1 was hospitalized,  and died
on October 9, 2017 due to the injuries sustained.
At 8:35 a.m. on October 9, 2017, Employee #1 was ascending a ladder to complete
ceiling preparation. Employee #1 fell from the ladder and fell to a concrete
surface below, injuring his neck and was killed.

shear. As the employee was feeding the machine, his finger bypassed the guard
and he sustained a partial amputation of his right index finger. Employee #1 was
hospitalized for treatment.

bound lanes of the I-76 PA Turnpike,  a vehicle with two passengers traveling

At 9:15 a.m. on October 12, 2017, Employee #1, employed by a construction

some merchandise when he was struck in the leg by the rear bumper of a forklift

At 7:15 a.m. on May 9, 2017, an employee was cutting a fallen tree when he cut

At 4:30 p.m. on September 29, 2017, Employee #1 was riding on a lawn mower. A

Employee #1 was transported to the hospital.  He was admitted and treated for

At 8:45 p.m. on August 6, 2017, an employee, a firefighter, was breaking through

pallets are 46 inches square, 7 feet 2 inches tall, and weigh about 1800 lbs.
The two employees asked a third employee to come help them when one of the

#3 up the ladder, which was a step ladder that was not opened fully, but leaned

using a stepladder incorrectly, over reaching from the ladder, not using a safe
means to access the high pile, not ensuring that forklift loads were secured
from tipping, and not stacking material so it doesn't create a hazard.

At 11:00 a.m. on January 22, 2019, an employee and his coworker were working at
a solid waste landfill in Victorville, CA. It was a permanent site. The employee
worked as a transfer driver. He delivered refuse to the dump or landfill. He was
operating a "big rig" truck and tractor trailer number 704 to dump trash at the
landfill. The employee and his coworker were fulltime employees of the employer.
The employee had parked his big rig. He was standing behind the rear door to the
trailer and unlatching it so that he could open it and dump the trash. His
coworker had parked next to the employee in a separate truck. As the coworker
was about to get out of his truck, he saw a large piece of wood or trash fall
out of top of the truck the employee was driving and strike the employee. It was
a wooden log was about 2 meters (77 inches, or 6.5 feet) long and 0.77 meters
(29 or 29.5 inches) in diameter. The truck's load had not been secured from
dangerous displacement. The employee suffered fractures to his right ankle, both
knees, ribs, head, back, vertebrae. He also suffered torn ligaments. He was
airlifted to Loma Linda Medical Hospital. DOSH learned about the incident by
telephone call from employer on January 25, 2019. The employer did not comply
with reporting requirements; the report was late. DOSH arrived at the site at
11:00 a.m. on February 12, 2019. The employer was cited for a violation of T8
CCR3704: Securing Loads. It was determined that prior to and during the course
of the investigation, including, but not limited to February 12, 2019, the
employer failed to secure the load from dangerous displacement. As a result, on
January 22, 2019 a transport driver was seriously injured when he was struck in
the head by a dislodged wooden log measuring 77 inches by 29.5 inches when he
attempted to open the trailer door on trailer #704 at the Victorville landfill.
The stump was also described as an 8-foot tree stump.
